newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends quiet day barely changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends quiet day barely changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended near unchanged in subdued dealings Monday, as producer-linked selling capped a light round of buying by speculators and the trade, brokers said.

Short-covering on the part of commodity funds lent some strength to the market, sustaining nearby March a notch above unchanged for much of the session. But origin selling intensified near the 10.70-mark, easily blocking a test of resistance toward 10.75-10.76.
Locals and the trade both sold the market ahead of the close, erasing the day's modest gains.
"The buying ran into trade selling from 10.70 cents up, and that put a lid on it," one trader said. "But all in all, it was a very quiet session."
Most-active March ended flat at 10.66 cents, having ranged from 10.63 to 10.71. Second-position May rose 0.01, to 10.74, as the switches remained fairly stable.
Turnover was scant, at an estimated 5,891 lots.

Technically, March would need to punch through 10.75 cents to sustain buying interest, chartists said. But with physical offtake likely to be limited through the end of the calendar year, the market could gravitate toward support at 10.50 cents in the near-term, they said.
-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
